Appreciate the details, Sarah 

this is super helpful. Below are quick, do-not-use-as-final back-of-envelope comparisons based on the profile you shared. I’ll have a more detailed spreadsheet and sensitivity scenarios by EOD tomorrow.

Assumptions (round numbers):
- Sustained: 50 RPS (avg), peaks 150 RPS (short windows)
- Avg tokens/request: 75
- Month length: 30 days

Estimated monthly tokens = 50 req/s * 86,400 s/day * 75 tokens = ~324M tokens/day -> ~9.7B tokens/month (sustained).

Hosted API (usage-based)
- Example rate: $0.0006 per token (model-dependent)
- Monthly cost (sustained): 9.7B * $0.0006 = ~$5.8M/month
- Pros: no infra management, elastic, immediate scale for peaks
- Cons: high cost at scale, less control over networking for strict VPC use cases

Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Example committed capacity pricing (illustrative):
  • Small commit (equivalent ~200 RPS sustained): $40k/month
  • Medium commit (~800 RPS): $140k/month
  • Large commit (multi-pool, HA): custom pricing — typically $300k+/month
- With Dedicated you buy GPU-backed capacity and get predictable throughput; effective per-token cost drops significantly for sustained high volume. Depending on model efficiency and batching, per-token economics can be an order of magnitude better vs hosted.
- Pros: predictable monthly bill, VPC peering and private networking options, better for sustained high throughput
- Cons: commit required, additional configuration for burst handling, procurement lead time

Private / On-prem
- One-time onboarding & infra setup + ongoing support/license fee. Higher TCO upfront but meets strictest compliance needs. Pricing typically requires an eval (we can provide an MSA + SOW).

Recommendations / next steps
1) We should run two scenarios in the model: (A) sustained 50 RPS with burst profile, and (B) seasonally varying traffic with peaks to 150 RPS. I’ll produce both with sensitivity to avg tokens and batching gains.
2) Technical deep-dive for Dedicated/Private: our infra team can cover VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log forwarding, and encryption-at-rest details. Lauren can lead that.
3) If you’re comfortable, share a 24‑72 hour sample of traffic logs (pseudonymized) so we can produce a tighter cost model.

I’ve attached the initial_pricing_estimates.xlsx with the simple calc shown above and a deployment_comparison_v1.pdf. Also attaching SOC2_summary.pdf for your security review.

Would Thursday or Friday work for a 45-min technical deep-dive?

Thanks,
Marcus
